page.title: Best 240V Portable Power Station (2026): Split-Phase Picks That Start a Well Pump
page.desc: Single-unit 120/240 V split-phase power stations compared on surge, capacity and maker-store price, with the cheapest 6,000 W pick and what owners complain about.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best 240V portable power station for most buyers is the OSCAL PowerMax 6000 ({buy:oscal-powermax-6000-3600wh-240v}): 6,000 W continuous and 9,000 W surge of split-phase 120/240 V from one unit, with 3,600 Wh of LiFePO4 storage, for about $1,000 or more less than any other 6,000 W split-phase unit sold on a maker store on 2026-11-06. Will it start a well pump? A 1 HP deep-well pump draws about 2,400 W running and up to 7,200 W starting, and the PowerMax 6000's 9,000 W surge covers that with room for a refrigerator and lights on the same unit.

Two honest exceptions. If 3,840 W is enough for your loads, the BLUETTI Apex 300 ({buy:bluetti-apex-300}) is the cheapest single-unit 240 V station we found, about $160 less, with 23% less capacity and a ship date in early December. If you are wiring a permanent whole-home backup and want the longest owner track record, the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 is the established choice at roughly $1,100 more; it was sold out on EcoFlow's US store on 2026-11-06.

Check three things before buying any of them. Your pump's nameplate: deep-well pumps are normally 240 V, shallow-well pumps are often 120 V. The receptacle you need: OSCAL does not say whether its 240 V outlet is a NEMA 14-50 or L14-30, so ask support before buying an inlet cord. And the weight: the PowerMax 6000 is 101 lb on wheels, a two-person lift into a truck.

cells.v240: Yes, split-phase; receptacle type not listed

page.after:
What owners complain about

Weight comes up more than anything else. Every true 240 V station on this page weighs about 100 lb or more. Reviewers of the PowerMax 6000 weighed it at 98 to 101 lb and called it a two-person lift, even with wheels and a pull handle.

Fan noise and idle drain are next. OSCAL's smaller PowerMax 1800 SE drained a full battery in about 1.5 days with AC and Wi-Fi left on, and its fan sometimes ran loudly with nothing plugged in. The PowerMax 6000 did better in a German lab test: fans were near silent while charging at 2,200 W and only audible above about 3,000 W of load. Turn AC output off when the unit sits idle.

The app is the weakest part of OSCAL's units. There is no OSCAL app. The station pairs through the generic Smart Life app, which shows power flow and charge limits and little else, and the 1800 SE's beeper cannot be silenced from it.

Capacity on the label is not capacity at the outlet. The same lab measured 2,960 Wh usable from the PowerMax 6000's 3,600 Wh rating on average across ports, about 82%, and only 66% at a slow 100 W AC load. Size the battery for a day of real runtime, not the sticker.

Pass-through limits bite the big names too. A long-term EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 owner found output capped near 1,800 W while plugged into shore power, and needed three resets in five weeks.

Transfer-switch trips. Any inverter can trip GFCI breakers when a transfer switch does not switch the neutral. Have an electrician check bonding before a permanent install, and never backfeed through a dryer outlet.

Which one by need

  • Well pump plus refrigerator in an outage, lowest price for 6,000 W: OSCAL PowerMax 6000. 9,000 W surge, 3,600 Wh, expansion to 57.6 kWh with BP3600 packs, 5-year warranty and 30-day returns. It was a pre-sale item on OSCAL's store on 2026-11-06 with shipping listed around November 26.
  • Lowest price and 3,840 W is enough: BLUETTI Apex 300 ({buy:bluetti-apex-300}). 2,764.8 Wh, 20 ms switchover, up to 58 kWh with packs, ships early December.
  • Most capacity in one 240 V unit: OUPES Guardian 6000 V2, 4,608 Wh and 6,000 W, $2,699 on the OUPES store on 2026-11-06.
  • Whole-home install with a transfer switch and the longest track record: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 or Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus. 4,096 Wh at 4,000 W and 3,840 Wh at 6,000 W, $2,799 and $2,999.99 on their US stores on 2026-11-06; the EcoFlow was sold out.
  • No 240 V loads, just the cheapest 3.6 kWh: OSCAL PowerMax 3600 SE ({buy:oscal-powermax-3600-se-3600wh}). Same capacity, 3,600 W, 120 V only.

Not recommended for 240 V

Anything with 240 in the name but 120 V output, such as the Jackery Explorer 240 line; it is a 256 Wh camping battery. Two-unit setups sold as 240 V, such as the Pecron E3600LFP, which needs two stations and a $99 connect box before it makes split-phase power. A 120 V station with a step-up transformer: it makes 240 V with no neutral, so dryer controls and anything with internal 120 V circuits will not work. And the OSCAL PowerMax 3600 SE for a well pump, since it lists no 240 V output.
